AUDIO: In 1998 the great Ennio Morricone had his score rejected by producers for the film "What Dreams May Come". No explanation was given and the film was rescored.
Come on, OP. It literally says it was rejected "in an attempt to have a more 'commercial' sound for the movie" right there on the page.
Feel free to find me an actual statement by the producers to that fact. That is simply what is surmised.
Maybe because it has a hint of the 'Streets of Cairo' song.

Whenever I hear of Hollywood decisions that are obscure (like an actor quitting a production over "artistic differences") I mentally tell myself that the real issue was money. IDK what happened here. But I can imagine a situation where, for example, the Big People were looking at the numbers, and decided to bring in a 2nd composer who would agree to fewer royalties than Ennio M. and (on paper) the studio makes more money on the film. Regardless, I can't imagine that they would think that they would make less money with the 2nd composer and go with him. Also looking at the other comments, I have difficulty imagining that Ennio M.'s sound would be considered 'uncommercial' given his credentials. He's made tons of soundtracks on successful films,so he's a proven horse so to speak.

I would imagine as the soundtrack was finished and they made the decision after the first screening, that it must have been an artistic decision. I would have trusted Ennio's artistic choices over the producers. He must have been paid most of the money since it was already finished, only losing out on some royalties.

I read elsewhere that Ennio was upset because not only did they not tell him why, but they didn't come to him and ask him to make changes. Instead they just hired another composer. Oh well. At least it wasn't a great film.

One thing I took away from that movie was the concept that "Hell is your life gone wrong". Great existential idea, but they visually represented it unrealistically as surrealistically heightened Gothic paintings come to life. Dark inverted cathedrals, ground paved with screaming faces etc. Nothing relate-able at all.

Later when I played Silent Hill 2 for the first time I realized that they'd nailed the visual (and aural - holy shit, those sounds) expression of "your life gone wrong". The familiar everyday world stained and rotting as a result of bad decisions and regret.

Still a big fan of Vincent Ward's "The Navigator". "Map of the Human Heart" is also worth checking out.

Anybody know where I can buy a 6-pack of Heavy Seas Loose Cannon around here?
That shouldn't be too hard to find. What part of town? Brawley's is my default recommendation, but there are probably other options closer to you.
Steele Creek area, right where I-485 intersects 160. I just moved here a few months ago and haven't found a craft beer store, or more accurately, haven't started looking for one yet.

I don't know of any shops over there, but I haven't been over there since before the outlet mall went in. There could be something new. If there's a Harris Teeter or Publix closer to you than Rivergate, check those first. Both tend to have above average (for a grocery store) craft selections.

If that fails, there's The Wine Shop in Rivergate, who will likely have it in a build-your-own-six-pack format, so it may be a bit more expensive. I can't remember if the prices on the bottles are for on-premises consumption or carry out, so if the price looks totally ridiculous that's probably the on-premises price. I think buying multiples gets you a discount as well.

A lot further down 160 into Fort Mill, SC, there's a shop in Baxter Village called The Grapevine. It's been a long time since I've been there, but I believe they still have a solid beer selection. Frugal MacDoogle is another option along the way at 160 and I-77, which is a combined beer/liquor store.

The next closest option is probably Good Bottle Co. at the corner of South and Remount. It's newish and I haven't been in there, but have heard some good things.

There's a much broader craft beer store selection here than even a few years ago, but Brawley's is one of the oldest and IMHO still the best. You should stop by there at some point for sure. Mike is a great guy who has done a lot to grow craft beer in the city. It's on Park Rd between Tyvola and Woodlawn, and not to be confused with Mike's Discount Beverages, which is next door.
